ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: <image>Find $E D$ if $A B=6, B C=4,$ and $A E=9$
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Geometry3K open-ended problem

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a large triangle ACD, A is at the lower left, C is at the upper left, D is at the upper right; point B is on side AC, point E is on side AD; segments BE and CD have arrow markings in the same direction, indicating that BE is parallel to CD. Then reason: Given by the problem AB=6, BC=4, so AC=AB+BC=10. Because BE is parallel to CD, triangle ABE and triangle ACD are similar, and corresponding sides satisfy AE/AD=AB/AC. It is known that AE=9, let ED=x, then AD=AE+ED=9+x. Substituting into the proportion gives 9/(9+x)=6/10. Cross multiply: 90=54+6x, so 36=6x, x=6. Therefore ED=6.
